html: Players often learn things the rest of the table does not know: what tiles the government saw, or what an investigation showed. You may always lie about hidden knowledge. The only time a player must tell the truth is in the game-ending Hitler situations: a player who is Hitler must say so if assassinated, or if elected Chancellor after three Fascist policies.

items: Everyone should claim to be a Liberal. The Liberal majority can shut out anyone who admits to being a Fascist. Liberals should usually tell the truth. They are solving a puzzle, and lying hurts their own team.

Hitler should be as Liberal as possible. Enact Liberal policies, vote for Liberal governments, and let the other Fascists create openings. Fascists win by quiet manipulation, not by playing openly evil.
Liberals gain from slowing down and discussing what is known. Fascists gain from rushed votes and confusion.
Fascists most often win by electing Hitler, not by six policies. It is the core of their strategy, so Hitler needs the Liberals' trust when the time comes.
Ask players to explain their actions, above all with powers. Ask a candidate in advance whom they would investigate, appoint or execute.
When a Fascist policy appears, there are only three possible culprits: the President, the Chancellor or the deck.
